summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever, left flank pain, and purulent drainage from his left nephrostomy tube, consistent with a genitourinary tract infection. He had recently completed treatment for a right foot cellulitis. Admission labs showed leukocytosis and elevated creatinine. Imaging revealed decompression of the renal collecting systems without abscess. Cultures from the nephrostomy tube and urine grew Group A Streptococcus and E. coli, guiding antibiotic therapy. Blood cultures showed coagulase-negative staph, likely a contaminant. He was started on meropenem and later transitioned to ertapenem via a PICC line for a two-week course. His infection resolved with normalization of vital signs and labs. A 5 mm left lung nodule was incidentally found on CT, requiring follow-up. He was discharged home with home health services for IV antibiotics and follow-up plans with urology and primary care.
